result.topic_en: A new proof of the Pythagorean theorem using isosceles triangles and similar triangles, with scattered marginal series expansions (arcsine and sine series) and some cipher-like scribbles.
result.transcription:
Math 32 \quad (1) [-48/1-]

Nova theorematis pythagoraei demonstratio

[cipher-like scribbles around a sketched right triangle, illegible]

[-$x + \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{3}x^3 + ...$-]
$x + \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{3}x^3 + \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{5}x^5 \ldots$ [?]
$x - \frac{1}{6}x^3 + \frac{1}{120}x^5 \ldots$ [?]
$\frac{\varpi}{\pi}\left(s + \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{3}s^3 + \frac{1\cdot 3}{2\cdot 4\cdot 5}s^5 \ldots\right)$ [?]
$\frac{\varpi}{\pi}s + \frac{1}{6}\frac{\varpi}{\pi}s^3 + \frac{3}{40}\frac{\varpi}{\pi}s^5 \ldots$
$- \frac{1}{6}\left(\frac{\varpi}{\pi}\right)^3$ [?]

[figure: right triangle ABC with right angle at A, AB produced to D and F, dashed lines CD, CF]

Theorema
Si trianguli ABC angulus A sit rectus erit $AB^{qu} + AC^{qu} = BC^{qu}$

$\frac{\varpi}{\pi}$

Demonstr. Producatur AB utrinque fiatque
$BD = BF = BC$. Tum triangula CBD, CBF erunt isosce-
lia, et anguli $BDC = BCD$; $BCF = BFC$.
At $BDC + DCB + BCF + CFB = 2$ Rectis
Quare $DCB + BCF$ erit = Recto. Hinc Angulus
[-...-]
$CDA = ACF$ et triangula ACD, AFC similia.
Quare $AC : AD = AF : AC$ et
$AC^{qu} = $ Rctg. [-...-] sub AD et AF i.e sub
$BC - AB$ et $BC + AB$. Hinc (Eucl. Elem. II.)
$AC^{qu} = BC^{qu} - AB^{qu}$ et $AC^{qu} + AB^{qu} = BC^{qu}$ QED

methods.what: Proof of the Pythagorean theorem: extend AB both ways with BD=BF=BC, use isosceles triangles to get angle DCF right, similar triangles ACD, AFC give AC^2 = AD·AF = (BC−AB)(BC+AB)
